items.statement: Across comparative studies, the excess haemolysis with cannula draws is concentrated in studies using standard vacuum tubes and untrained collectors, and is small (odds ratio below 1.5) when low-vacuum tubes or syringes are used.
items.rationale: Explains the conflict (c1, c2, c3) and would support a technique change rather than a ban.
items.risks: Too few studies per technique subgroup; technique poorly reported.

items.statement: Transport by high-speed pneumatic tube accounts for part of the emergency excess independent of collection method.
items.rationale: Supported by the tube speed study (c4).

items.statement: In children, cannula draws haemolyse less often than capillary samples, so avoiding cannula draws would not reduce paediatric haemolysis.
items.rationale: Suggested only by an undated abstract.

summary: Three hypotheses; h1 selected because it addresses the conflict directly.
